doc.title: Tommy Newsom and Ross Tompkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Eddie Condon's group without a bass player
summary: Ross led a group at Eddie Condon's around 1965 with no bass, and Tommy sat in.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well once in a while you’d come and sit in with us at Eddie Condon’s. I remember that.
Yeah, no I used to do that.

See he was already with the Tonight Show. I wasn’t yet. In about 1965 I was working at Eddie Condon’s. I had a very good group. It was myself, no bass player, Cliff Leeman was the drummer, Cutty Cutshall, great trombone player, Peanuts Hucko on clarinet and either Buck Clayton or Yank Lawson on trumpet. So that was good. And Tommy used to come and sit in with us once in a while.
You must have had to develop a pretty good left hand thing if you were working without a bass player?
Yeah. Every other place in New York had a bass player except Condon’s — no bass.
Is that because the ceiling is too low? I heard some clubs in New York, I don’t know—
Yeah that’s strange why they did that.
